anchors: reported instead as ONE SEVERE unsafe-input finding
decision: An uncompiled regex in a hot function is MEDIUM and in a non-hot function MINOR, on the generic scale; more patterns than the re cache holds stays MEDIUM with the recompile named; a pattern built from untrusted input is reported instead as one SEVERE unsafe-input finding.

evidence.text: measured 2026-11-08 on Python 3.14.4: re.match(literal) 240 ns vs compiled 130 ns per call, re._MAXCACHE 512. GREEN opus and haiku classified the hot case MEDIUM; a haiku re-probe on the cache-thrash text gave MEDIUM for 3,000 fixed patterns and SEVERE for user-built ones, guessing one-vs-two findings, which the final wording now states.

reopen_if: a profile shows uncompiled regex calls dominating a hot path's time on real input
why: The re module caches compiled patterns, so the call pays a lookup, a measurable hot-path cost that cannot exhaust time; SEVERE on the generic scale means it can.

anchors: Before reporting such a call as a hot spot, time it with `time.perf_counter()` around the call
decision: Cumulative profile time sitting in a thread join, queue get, lock or executor shutdown is timed with perf_counter in fresh interpreters without cProfile before it is reported as a hot spot.

evidence.text: A logging runtime shutdown charged 91 ms per CLI run under cProfile took 1-2 ms timed directly on real runs.

reopen_if: A profiler that attributes waits separately from work becomes the default tool of this skill.
why: The profiler slows the other thread, so a wait is charged far more than it costs without the profiler.

anchors: The same holds for a record (a NamedTuple, a dataclass) built around such a container
decision: A record (NamedTuple, dataclass) built around a container the function made is treated like a returned container: not a cache candidate as is.

evidence.text: A finder-reported function returning a NamedTuple holding a dict broke rendering under a bare lru_cache because a caller edits the dict; test_a_record_built_around_a_new_mutable_container_is_not_a_candidate fails on the pre-fix finder.

reopen_if: The finder learns to see through lower-case factories, or lru_cache gains copy-on-return.
why: The cached record is one object, so its container field is shared by every caller and one caller's edit changes later results.

anchors: measure a second cached arm that hands each caller a copy
decision: When a cached run fails because a caller edits the returned object, report the behaviour change and measure a cached arm that returns a copy per call before the verdict.

evidence.text: A copy-per-call arm gave the real answer for one candidate: 64.6 percent hits, no speed gain against the plain function.

reopen_if: profile_with_cache_template.py gains a built-in copy-per-call arm.
why: Without the copy arm the verdict is about behaviour, not speed, and a cache that wins only without the copy is not a real win.

anchors: a one-slot cache keyed by object identity removes the repeats with bounded memory
decision: Repeated decoding of one immutable, unhashable parsed node is removed with a one-slot identity cache stored as one tuple, valid only when the result depends on the node alone and the node is frozen all the way down.

evidence.text: A one-slot cache on a decoded module cut export CPU from 23.9-24.6 s to 21.3-21.6 s interleaved and pinned, byte-identical output, mutation-tested.

reopen_if: A measurement shows the identity check missing repeats (readers receive equal but distinct nodes).
why: It avoids hashing the tree, keeps memory bounded, and a single tuple keeps a free-threaded reader from pairing one node with another's result.

anchors: keep the entries in a scratch file and write them into the file once you can reach it
decision: A declined finding whose instructions file cannot be written from the current workspace is kept in a scratch file and written once the file is reachable.

evidence.text: An Edit of the main checkout's untracked CLAUDE.md was refused from a worktree-isolated session, and the worktree held no copy.

reopen_if: The decline record moves out of the project instructions file.
why: An isolated worktree has no copy of an untracked CLAUDE.md and an edit of the main checkout's copy can be refused; the skill gave no route, so the decline was at risk of being lost.
